chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, raising it, who said:

A woman asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and said: “I used to remain seated during my nifās for twenty days, until they gave me a ruling of eighteen days.” So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “And why did they give you a ruling of eighteen days?”

A man said: “Because of the hadith that was narrated from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, that he said to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays when she had postpartum bleeding after giving birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr.” Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when eighteen days had already come for her; and had she asked him before that, he would have ordered her to perform ghusl and to act as the mustaḥāḍah acts.”

key_terms.أَفْتَوْنِي: they gave me a juristic ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, whose bleeding is treated differently from ḥayḍ and nifās
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا: eighteen days mentioned in the legal discussion of nifās
key_terms.نُفِسَتْ: she experienced postpartum bleeding after childbirth
key_terms.نِفَاسِي: my state of postpartum bleeding after childbirth

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith prove that nifās lasts eighteen days?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling of nifās and clarifies that the report concerning Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays does not establish eighteen days as a fixed rule. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that she only asked after eighteen days had passed, and that if she had asked earlier, she would have been instructed to perform ghusl and follow the ruling of the mustaḥāḍah.
